objective: MIND (Sliced Wasserstein on Inception-v3 features), lower is better
noise_sd_note: run-to-run spread of one configuration, from 8 replicate pairs in the discrete study
dataset: celeba_dynamic_t_v2 b0+b5 variant, 500 clean + 26014 blurred (sigma_blur=0.5), 26514 annotations
probe: 160 holdout images x 2 noise draws x 20 T levels, every 100 kimg; see training/probe.py
curve_note: knots = piecewise-linear control points over training fraction; constant = static T; log = applied T read from the committed probe log (null T_applied means the hold was in force and the run trained at T=0)

runs.name: warmup40
runs.note: best of the 30-run discrete search; argmin, so optimistically biased

runs.name: gt_warmup
runs.note: same schedule as warmup_0to095 with the probe attached but not steering; +0.96 sd apart, so probing is non-invasive

runs.name: pr_predvar_hold25
runs.note: T held at 0 for the first 25%, then probe-driven. Refuted the first-quarter hypothesis.

runs.name: pr_predvar
runs.note: headline run, n=2. Predicted in advance to fall in 0.0335-0.0350. Pooled static (n=2) is 0.035083, i.e. -0.19 sd -- indistinguishable.

runs.name: gt_static50
runs.note: probe attached, not steering; +0.40 sd from static_T050

runs.name: pr_predvar_nosmooth
runs.note: identical to pr_predvar except alpha 0.3 -> 1.0; +2.11 sd worse, isolating the smoother

runs.name: pr_msegap
runs.note: worst of all 40 runs; calibration predicted it would be degenerate

runs.name: pr_predvar_hold50
runs.note: T held at 0 for the first 50%. Refuted the 'suppress the probe early' fix: still 3.3 sd worse than warmup.
